questions.stem: A 3-year-old with these findings — a brown macule (cafe-au-lait spot) on the trunk and a malformed thumb — together with pancytopenia most likely has which condition?

explanation.summary: Cafe-au-lait spots with skin hypopigmentation, short stature, and radial/thumb anomalies accompanying progressive pancytopenia are classic for Fanconi anemia, an autosomal recessive DNA-repair defect that causes inherited bone marrow failure.
explanation.whyCorrect: Cafe-au-lait spots with skin hypopigmentation, short stature, and radial/thumb anomalies accompanying progressive pancytopenia are classic for Fanconi anemia, an autosomal recessive DNA-repair defect that causes inherited bone marrow failure.

questions.stem: This schematic maps the differentiation of a single precursor into all blood cell types. In aplastic anemia the marrow defect shown here spares one branch relatively — cells of which lineage are LEAST reduced?

explanation.summary: Aplastic anemia is caused by loss of myeloid hematopoietic stem cells, so RBCs, platelets, granulocytes, and monocytes all fall (pancytopenia). Lymphoid progenitors arise from a separate branch of this scheme and are relatively preserved, so lymphocyte counts remain near normal on a CBC.
